entries.reasoning: Reading endocrine.sh cmd_propagate_downstream (lines 767-780): the propagation formula is `to.dopamine += (from.dopamine - 0.5) × 0.3`. At from.dopamine = 0.7 (exploration baseline), delta = (0.7-0.5)×0.3 = 0.06. At from.dopamine = 0.9 (high after multiple gate passes), delta = 0.12. This is a small but non-trivial increment. The cortisol contagion fires only if from.cortisol > 0.8 (high stress state). At the build archetype cortisol baseline of 0.5, contagion would not fire unless multiple gate failures drove cortisol above 0.8. This means NS-003 ESCALATED events (on_gate_fail → cortisol +0.10 per failure) could trigger contagion after ~3 consecutive escalations in build agents. This is an emergent system behavior from the endocrine design that is relevant to NS-003 ConflictSignal frequency expectations.
implications: If NS-003 generates frequent ConflictSignals in build phase (multiple ESCALATED per run), cortisol contagion cascades are a risk — system-wide stress increase
CCR measurement should track how many ConflictSignals reach ESCALATED vs resolved, to estimate endocrine impact

entries.section: Potential Unknown Unknowns — COMMANDER integration complexity

If agents write their own outputs directly (via tool calls within their LLM context), there may be no interception point at the COMMANDER level. implications: Before designing NS-003 COMMANDER integration, must audit the exact mechanism by which agent outputs become artifact files

entries.section: NS-003-B Pre-Commit vs Post-Hoc Interface Flag (FR-NS3B-004)
entries.reasoning: IS-003 (SAGE WHY1) identified that the write-time interception mechanism in COMMANDER is architecturally unresolved. The two candidate models (Model A: COMMANDER-controlled write; Model B: write-wrapper utility) have incompatible implementation strategies. Rather than resolving this in the WHAT phase (which would constitute an architecture decision, violating the NEVER rules), FR-NS3B-004 requires the ns003_agm.py module to implement BOTH modes via the --mode [pre-commit|post-hoc] interface flag, with post-hoc as the default. This design is explicitly neutral on which model is ultimately used and defers the architectural choice to HOW. The default to post-hoc ensures the module is immediately usable regardless of how IS-003 resolves. OQ-001 tracks this as the highest-priority HOW-phase concern.
implications: HOW phase must make the Model A vs Model B decision as the first NS-003 architecture task
If Model A is infeasible (agents self-write), pre-commit mode requires a write-wrapper utility that modifies every agent prompt
